title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: the 'équation des lacets' part of the Longue Marche continuation. The context points to the SL2(Z)/B3-type picture, with the profinite group π̂ carrying elements ρ and σ whose (normalised) centralisers L_ρ and L_σ are cyclic of orders 6 and 4. Their common part μ = L_ρ∩π̂ = L_σ∩π̂ = {±1} is the centre, of order 2 (formula (57) on the previous page). M^![0] = Z^!_{ρ,σ} is a group of 'automorphisms' u (Galois/GT-type elements) acting by u(ρ)=int(α)ρ, u(σ)=int(β)σ. The group SoΓ^!_{ρ,σ} consists of triples (u,a,b) with a∈N_ρ, b∈N_σ.

The previous page proved two things:
- So^πΓ^! is a subgroup surjecting onto Z^!.
- Its kernel is {(1,a,b)} with a∈L_ρ, b∈L_σ.

Corollary on this page:
1. SoΓ^!_{ρ,σ} is an extension of Z^!_{ρ,σ} by the abelian group L_ρ×L_σ ≅ Z/6×Z/4.
2. Splitting Z/6 = Z/3×Z/2 by CRT, with the Z/2 identified with μ, the kernel is μ×L'_ρ×L_σ ≅ Z/2×Z/3×Z/4.
3. An extension by a direct product of abelian kernels is the fibre product of its three pushout extensions. So it corresponds canonically to three extensions, by μ, by L_ρ (the Z/3 part) and by L_σ.
4. The extensions by L_ρ and L_σ have canonical sections, given by the normalisations via (51) and the CRT splitting.
5. What remains is one genuine extension of Z^! by μ = {±1}, namely So^πΓ^!_{ρ,σ}.

Interpretation: this μ-extension encodes the sign ambiguity in lifting α̃∈π̂/±1 (determined by u) to α∈π̂. Equivalently it is the sign ambiguity of a∈N_ρ, via (58): a = ξ_3(21)α^{-1}u, α = u a^{-1} ξ_3(21).

The ambiguity had been removed by the normalisation α∈π̂_{0,2τ} = F̂_{{1,2}}·π̂_3. The page announces that this set-theoretic section is not multiplicative. The next page computes the defect: α'' = εα'α with ε = -1 exactly when ε_3(u) = -1 and ε_2(u')ε_3(u') = +1. This is an explicit 2-cocycle with values in ±1 describing how the Galois/GT action on the 'PSL2 level' lifts to the 'SL2 level' (central ±1).
errors: Minor: the decomposition presupposes the product of the extension by the abelian kernel L_ρ×L_σ behaves as a direct product of pushouts. This is fine for abelian kernels, but the identification of μ with the Z/2 factor of L_ρ (rather than inside L_σ ≅ Z/4) is a choice, not canonical without the context of (57).
The claim that the L_ρ- and L_σ-extensions 'admettent des sections canoniques' is asserted without argument on this page. It presumably rests on the normalisation of a, b via (51) earlier.

ideas.what: Decomposing an extension with abelian kernel Z/6×Z/4 into three pushout extensions by Z/2, Z/3, Z/4 (CRT), and identifying canonical sections of two of them
ideas.modern_name: Pushout/Baer decomposition of extensions with product kernel

ideas.what: The residual extension by μ={±1} measures the sign ambiguity in lifting inner automorphism data from π̂/±1 to π̂. A convenient normalisation α∈F̂_{1,2}·π̂_3 is shown to be non-multiplicative, with an explicit ±1 cocycle given on the next page.
ideas.modern_name: Lifting the GT/Galois action from P̂SL2(Z) (or B̂3 mod centre) to the central extension, and the associated ±1 cocycle
ideas.usually_credited_to: Lifts of GT action to B̂3 / ŜL2: Drinfeld 1990, Ihara, Lochak–Schneps, Nakamura (various 1990s papers)

missed.claim: Grothendieck identifies the obstruction to a multiplicative normalisation of the lifts α as a ±1-extension. On the following page he computes the cocycle explicitly in terms of characters ε_2, ε_3. This is an explicit sign rule for composing normalised lifts that I do not recall in this exact form in the GT literature.
missed.quote: Il reste une extension (c'est justement So^πΓ^!_{ρ,σ}) de Z^!_{ρ,σ} par μ. Cette extension correspond justement à l'ambiguïté de signes
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Explicit cocycles for the action on the central ±1 of ŜL2(Z)/B̂3 are relevant to comparing GT actions on B̂3 versus P̂SL2 and on modular-curve towers. However, analogous results likely exist in some form (Nakamura, Lochak–Schneps), so novelty is uncertain.

deep.surprise_reason: Technical, correct bookkeeping of a central ±1 extension in the lacet-equation setting. The explicit non-multiplicativity cocycle (next page) is a nice unpublished detail but close in spirit to known lifts of GT actions to B̂3/ŜL2.
transcription_corrections: Top page number reads more plausibly '600' than '500', given the references to pp. 597', 598 on the neighbouring pages.
'Z^{!←}_{ρ,σ}' is just Z^!_{ρ,σ}; the arrow is a stray mark or insertion sign.
The crossed-out passage in the parenthesis is something like 'L_ρ ≃ μL'_ρ × μ'; the intended statement is L_ρ ≃ Z/3×Z/2.
